Angular_Leaf_Spot.quote: As the disease progresses, the infected spots turn brown and the leaf material falls out, leaving angular holes in the leaves.
On fruit the bacterium causes circular spots which often crack open and turn white in color.

Anthracnose.quote: The disease can develop on all aboveground parts of cucumber and cause leaf spot, blight, stem canker, and fruit rot during the growing season.
When stems and petioles are infected, symptoms start as elongated, oval to diamond-shaped light brown cankers.

Bacterial_Wilt.quote: Individual runners or whole cucumber plants wilt and die rapidly, with symptoms appearing at any growth stage but most often noticed early in the season while plants are growing rapidly.
Leaves typically turn a dull green color, and progressive wilting of lateral leaves occurs.

Belly_Rot.quote: Water-soaked, tan to brown lesions, which become sunken, cratered, irregular, and dried as they enlarge appear on the undersides and blossom ends of cucumber fruit.

Corynespora_Leaf_Spot.quote: Target spot begins on leaves as yellow leaf flecks, which later become angular with a definite outline.

Downy_Mildew.quote: Downy mildew causes angular, yellow to brown lesions on top of the leaves that are restricted by leaf veins.

Gummy_Stem_Blight.quote: Leaf symptoms appear as dark yellow or reddish brown lesions of various shapes. Lesions begin at leaf margins but rapidly extend back into the leaf blade, causing curling, shriveling, and leaf death.
On the lesions, golden-brown gummy drops occur, hence the name gummy stem blight.

Phytophthora_Blight.quote: Symptoms on cucumber are normally found on leaves and fruit, rather than crown rot which is more common on squash and pumpkins.
Lesions on stems are constricted, darkened, and water-soaked, often extending a few inches above the soil line.
Whole plants or vines collapse quickly.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: Upper and lower leaf surfaces and stems are typically affected.
Powdery mildew first appears as pale yellow spots on stems, petioles, and leaves, which enlarge as the white, fluffy mycelium grows over plant surfaces.
